challenges.documentation:
FIELD BRIEF — Door Status API (fictional)

Objective:
Unlock the exit by retrieving the status of this room's exit door.

Resources:
- Door panels are resources under /api/doors/{doorId}.
- {doorId} is the door's facility label in lowercase (the exit door in this room is labeled Alpha).

Method semantics:
- GET retrieves the current representation of a resource. Use GET when you only need to read status.
- POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE create or change resources and are not appropriate for a simple status check.

Rules:
- No request body is required for a status retrieval.
- Build the method and full resource path yourself from these rules. The terminal will not paste the completed request for you.

FIELD BRIEF — Door Status API (fictional)

Objective:

Resources:
- Door panels are resources under /api/doors/{doorId}.
- {doorId} is the door's facility label in lowercase (this verification panel is labeled Bravo).

Method semantics:
- GET retrieves status. Prefer GET for read-only checks.
- Write methods (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) are not used for status retrieval.

Rules:
- No request body is required.
- Construct method and path independently from these rules.

FIELD BRIEF — Lock Locator API (fictional)

Objective:
Locate the active lock for this room so the exit can open.

Resources:
- Locks live under /api/locks/{lockId}.
- {lockId} is a path parameter: replace the braces with the lock's facility code. Do not leave {lockId} literally in the request.
- Facility codes use lowercase words joined by hyphens (pattern: <direction>-gate).
- This room's active lock is the north gate.

Method semantics:
- GET reads lock state. Use GET when locating or checking a lock.
- Write methods are not required for this check.

Rules:
- No query string or body is required.
- Choose the method and assemble the path with the correct substituted lock id.

challenges.documentation:
FIELD BRIEF — Sensor Filter API (fictional)

Objective:
Clear the exit by filtering sensors for the zone assigned to this terminal.

Resources:
- Sensors are listed at /api/sensors.
- Filtering uses a query string after ?: name=value.

Method semantics:
- GET retrieves a filtered list. Use GET for read/filter operations.

Parameter rules:
- Required query parameter name: zone
- Zone values are lowercase sector codes used in this facility (Alpha sector → alpha, Bravo sector → bravo).
- This terminal is assigned to the Alpha sector.
- Illustrative shape only (you must choose the real values): /api/sensors?zone=<sector>

Rules:
- No request body is required.
- Select the method and build the full path plus query yourself.

successBody.message: Zone bravo sensors cleared the door.

Objective:
Activate the primary registration terminal by submitting the checkpoint registration.

Resources:
- Registrations are submitted under /api/registrations/{checkpointId}.
- {checkpointId} is the lowercase facility label for this panel (alpha).

Method semantics:
- POST submits a new registration for the checkpoint.
- GET retrieves existing records and will not activate this panel.
- PUT/PATCH/DELETE are not used for first-time registration here.

Rules:
- No query string is required.
- Module 1 grades method and path only — leave the body blank unless docs later require fields.
- Construct method and path yourself from these rules.

FIELD BRIEF — Clearance Update API (fictional)

Objective:
Update the north-desk clearance so the exit route can open.

Resources:
- Clearance records live under /api/clearances/{clearanceId}.
- Substitute {clearanceId} with the facility code (this panel: north-desk).
- Do not leave braces in the submitted path.

Method semantics:
- PUT fully updates the existing clearance record.
- PATCH is a related partial-update idea covered in training; this panel expects PUT.
- GET reads without updating. POST creates new records and is wrong here.

Rules:
- No query string is required.
- Construct method and path with the substituted id yourself.
